title: Alleles inherited together more than expected: linkage disequilibrium
vignette: A study is undertaken to map the HLA-DQ loci in a population with a high incidence of celiac sprue. High-resolution HLA typing of the DQA1 and DQB1 loci is performed using polymerase chain reaction sequencing. The frequency of the DQA1*0501-DQB1*0201 haplotype, strongly implicated in autoimmunity, is found to be 0.2. However, in the same population, the frequency of the DQA1*0501 allele is 0.3 and the frequency of the DQB1*0201 allele is 0.2. Which of the following best explains the observed DQA1*0501-DQB1*0201 haplotype frequency in this population?

clues.text: frequency of the DQA1*0501-DQB1*0201 haplotype, strongly implicated in autoimmunity, is found to be 0.2
clues.note: The observed haplotype (two specific alleles inherited together) frequency is 0.2 - much higher than random pairing would predict, the signature of linkage disequilibrium.

clues.text: frequency of the DQA1*0501 allele is 0.3 and the frequency of the DQB1*0201 allele is 0.2
clues.note: If the two alleles were inherited independently, the expected haplotype frequency = 0.3 x 0.2 = 0.06. The observed 0.2 far exceeds 0.06, so the alleles are NOT independent.

whatMatters: The two alleles are inherited together far more often than chance predicts: observed haplotype frequency 0.2 vs expected 0.3 x 0.2 = 0.06. Alleles at different loci co-occurring more (or less) often than expected from their individual frequencies = LINKAGE DISEQUILIBRIUM (here from the close proximity of HLA-DQA1 and HLA-DQB1). Answer C.
strategy: Do the math: expected haplotype frequency under independence = product of allele frequencies (0.3 x 0.2 = 0.06). Observed (0.2) >> expected (0.06) means the alleles are non-randomly associated = linkage disequilibrium. Reject the mitochondrial (heteroplasmy), single-gene (penetrance, pleiotropy), and normal-segregation options - none explains a nonrandom two-locus haplotype excess.

eliminations.label: Heteroplasmy - mitochondrial
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: heteroplasmy is the presence of different mitochondrial genomes (mutant and wild-type) within a cell. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it concerns mitochondrial DNA, not the co-inheritance of two nuclear HLA alleles. ✅ Correct if: mitochondrial disease variability.

eliminations.label: Increased penetrance - genotype-to-phenotype
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: penetrance is the proportion of people with a genotype who express its phenotype. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's about phenotypic expression, not the frequency of a two-allele haplotype. ✅ Correct if: describing how often a genotype manifests.

eliminations.label: Pleiotropy - one gene, many effects
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a single gene causing multiple phenotypic manifestations. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: unrelated to haplotype frequency/co-inheritance. ✅ Correct if: one mutation with multi-organ effects (e.g., Marfan).

eliminations.label: Segregation - normal allele separation, your pick
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the law of segregation describes paired alleles separating so each gamete gets one. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: normal segregation would predict independent (product-rule) haplotype frequencies - it does NOT explain the EXCESS co-inheritance observed. ✅ Correct if: describing basic Mendelian gamete formation.

reasoning: Expected haplotype frequency if independent = 0.3 x 0.2 = 0.06
Observed haplotype frequency = 0.2, much greater than 0.06
The two alleles are inherited together more often than chance predicts
-> linkage disequilibrium (HLA-DQA1 and DQB1 are physically close); answer C
mechanism: Two alleles at different loci are said to be in LINKAGE DISEQUILIBRIUM when they are inherited together in the same gamete (as a haplotype) more - or less - often than expected by chance given their individual allele frequencies. The expected haplotype frequency under independence is the product of the two allele frequencies (here 0.3 x 0.2 = 0.06); the observed frequency (0.2) greatly exceeds this, so the alleles are non-randomly associated. Linkage disequilibrium most often reflects physical proximity of the loci on the same chromosome (as with the closely situated HLA-DQA1 and HLA-DQB1 genes encoding the alpha and beta chains of the class II MHC molecule), so recombination rarely separates them. The distractors describe mitochondrial variability (heteroplasmy), genotype-to-phenotype expression (penetrance), one gene with many effects (pleiotropy), and normal Mendelian allele separation (segregation) - none explains an excess two-locus haplotype frequency.

difficulty.label: 📚 Pure knowledge gap
difficulty.message: First Aid Genetics > linkage disequilibrium: alleles co-inherited more/less than expected from allele frequencies; often due to physical proximity; HLA haplotypes; Hardy-Weinberg (2pq) doesn't apply across loci.

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: Compute the expected (product-rule) haplotype frequency and compare to the observed excess to name the phenomenon.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on haplotype, allele frequency, linkage disequilibrium, penetrance, pleiotropy, or segregation? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: Segregation (your pick) predicts INDEPENDENT (product-rule) frequencies; the observed EXCESS is linkage disequilibrium. Heteroplasmy/penetrance/pleiotropy are unrelated concepts.

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: observed haplotype frequency > product of allele frequencies (0.2 > 0.06) = linkage disequilibrium (loci in close proximity).

keywords.front: Alleles co-inherited more/less than expected from their frequencies

keywords.back: Physical proximity of loci on the same chromosome (little recombination)
Different mitochondrial genomes within a cell
Proportion with a genotype who express the phenotype
